html:
British Somaliland was a British protectorate on the Gulf of Aden coast of the Horn of Africa, in what is now Somaliland. The map shows it from 1914 to 1945.

Britain took it in the 1880s mainly to supply meat to its port of Aden across the water. It signed treaties with the Somali clans and ran the territory cheaply from Berbera and Hargeisa. From 1899 to 1920 the Dervish movement of Mohammed Abdullah Hassan fought the British, until a campaign using aircraft broke it in 1920.

In the Second World War Italy, which held Italian Somaliland and Ethiopia, occupied the protectorate in August 1940; Britain retook it in 1941.

British Somaliland became independent on 26 June 1960 and five days later joined the former Italian territory to form Somalia. When Somalia collapsed in 1991, the north declared itself the independent Republic of Somaliland within the old protectorate's borders. It has won little formal recognition abroad.
sum: British Somaliland was a British protectorate on the Gulf of Aden coast of the Horn of Africa, in what is now Somaliland. The map shows it from 1914 to 1945.
